name: units-invalid-for-unit-class
description: A tag has a value with units that are invalid or not of the correct unit class for the tag.
common_causes: Using units not defined in schema
Wrong unit class for the tag
Incorrect unit abbreviations
Missing space between value and unit
Applying unit modifiers to non-SI units
explanation: HED tags requiring units must use valid units from the appropriate unit class. Units must be spelled correctly, properly spaced from values, and compatible with the tag's requirements.
correction_strategy: Use valid units from correct unit classes

correction_examples.explanation: Used correct acceleration unit instead of time unit
Used correct weight unit instead of time unit
Added required space between value and unit

correction_patterns: Check schema for valid units in tag's unit class
Ensure proper spacing (value + space + unit)
Use standard SI units when possible
Apply unit modifiers only to SI units
Match unit class to tag requirements
fix_instructions: 1. Identify the tag's required unit class from schema
2. Check if current unit exists in that unit class
3. Replace with valid unit if needed
4. Ensure proper spacing between value and unit
5. Verify unit modifiers are used correctly
validation_hints: Consult schema unit classes for valid units
Check spacing between numbers and units
Verify unit class matches tag requirements
Ensure unit modifiers only with SI units

name: units-invalid-si-units
description: A unit modifier is applied to units that are not SI units.
common_causes: Applying SI prefixes (k, m, etc.) to non-SI units
Using modifiers like 'kilo' with imperial units
Confusion about which units support SI prefixes
Attempting to modify units that don't allow modification
explanation: SI unit modifiers (like kilo-, milli-, micro-) can only be applied to SI base units. Applying them to non-SI units like feet creates invalid unit combinations.
correction_strategy: Use SI units with modifiers or remove modifiers from non-SI units

correction_examples.explanation: Changed to SI unit (kilometer) instead of modifying non-SI unit
Converted to proper SI unit with conversion
Used proper SI abbreviation for kilometers

correction_patterns: Convert to proper SI units with modifiers
Remove invalid modifiers from non-SI units
Use standard SI prefix abbreviations
fix_instructions: 1. Identify units with invalid modifiers
2. Check if unit is SI-compatible
3. Either convert to SI unit or remove modifier
4. Use standard prefix abbreviations (k, m, μ, etc.)
validation_hints: Check if unit accepts SI prefixes
Verify modifier applies to SI base unit
Ensure proper prefix abbreviation format

name: units-invalid-case
description: Units are case-sensitive: a unit name, unit symbol, or SI modifier written in a case other than the one listed in the schema is invalid.
common_causes: Capitalizing a unit name at the start of a value (Seconds, Feet)
Capitalizing an SI modifier (Milliseconds instead of milliseconds)
Writing a unit symbol in the wrong case (MS for ms, hz for Hz)
Assuming units follow the case-insensitive rule that applies to tags
explanation: HED tags are case-insensitive, but units are not. Every unit string - the unit name, the unit symbol, and any SI modifier - must match the schema exactly. This is what keeps m (milli) distinct from M (mega) and mV distinct from MV.
correction_strategy: Write the unit exactly as it appears in the schema, including any SI modifier

correction_examples.explanation: The modifier milli is lowercase
Unit names are written as listed in the schema
The symbol for millisecond is ms; MS is not a unit
The hertz symbol is Hz

correction_patterns: Lowercase unit names and modifiers
Match symbol case exactly (Hz, ms, uV, km)
Do not capitalize a unit because it starts the value
fix_instructions: 1. Find the unit in the schema unit class listing
2. Copy its spelling and case exactly
3. If an SI modifier is used, write it as listed (milli, k, u), never capitalized
validation_hints: Compare the unit string to the schema with case preserved
Check the modifier prefix separately from the base unit
Symbols and names are both case-sensitive

name: units-invalid-symbol-plural
description: A unit symbol cannot be pluralized, and a unit name accepts only the plural that the specification lists for it.
common_causes: Adding s to a unit symbol (mss, Hzs)
Adding s to a unit whose plural is itself (hertzs)
Guessing a plural instead of using the listed one (foots instead of feet)
explanation: Unit names such as second or foot may be written in the plural that the unit plurals file of the specification lists for them (seconds, feet); no plural is derived by a rule. Unit symbols such as ms and Hz are abbreviations that already stand for singular and plural and take no s. Hertz is its own plural.
correction_strategy: Use the singular symbol, or the plural that the specification lists for the unit name

correction_examples.explanation: Hertz is both singular and plural
Symbols are never pluralized
Symbols are never pluralized

correction_patterns: Never pluralize a symbol
Use the plural that the unit plurals file lists for a unit name
When unsure, use the singular form
fix_instructions: 1. Check whether the unit is a symbol (short abbreviation such as ms, Hz, km) or a name (second, foot, hertz)
2. For a symbol, remove any trailing s
3. For a name, use the plural that the unit plurals file of the specification lists for it, or the singular
validation_hints: Symbols match only their exact string
Names match their singular and the one plural listed for them
hertz is its own listed plural

name: units-invalid-plural-not-listed
description: The plural of a unit name is the one that the unit plurals file of the specification lists for it; a unit name with an SI unit modifier takes the modifier followed by that plural, and no other plural is valid.
common_causes: Adding s or es to a unit name that has an irregular or compound plural (foots, inchs, degree-Celsiuses)
Adding s to a unit name whose plural is itself (kilohertzs)
Pluralizing a unit name that the schema in use does not define (Volts in schema 8.5.0 is not a unit)
Adding an ending to the last component of a compound name instead of using the listed plural (millidegree-Celsiuses adds es to Celsius; the listed plural pluralizes degree: millidegrees-Celsius)
explanation: No plural is derived by a rule. The plural of a unit name is the one the unit plurals file of the HED specification lists for it: feet for foot, inches for inch, degrees-Celsius for degree-Celsius, and hertz for hertz. A unit name with an SI unit modifier takes the modifier followed by the listed plural (millidegrees-Celsius, kilohertz). A string that is not the listed plural of a unit name of the schema in use is not a valid unit.
correction_strategy: Use the singular unit name or the plural that the specification lists for it; with an SI unit modifier, put the modifier before the listed plural

correction_examples.explanation: The listed plural of degree-Celsius is degrees-Celsius
A modified plural is the modifier followed by the listed plural
The listed plural of foot is feet
The listed plural of inch is inches
Hertz is its own plural, so kilohertz is too
Unit names are case-sensitive and the unit name of schema 8.5.0 is volt, whose plural is volts

correction_patterns: Look up the plural of a unit name in the unit plurals file instead of guessing it
Put an SI unit modifier before the listed plural
When unsure, use the singular form
fix_instructions: 1. Find the singular unit name that the string is a plural of
2. Check that the schema in use defines that unit name
3. Replace the string with the plural that the unit plurals file lists for that name, or with the singular
4. If the string has an SI unit modifier, keep the modifier in front of the listed plural
validation_hints: A unit name matches its singular and the one plural listed for it
A unit name that is not listed has no plural
An entry of the plurals file applies only if its key is a unit name of the schema in use
specification_reference: 3.1.4.4. Unit classes and units; A.8. Unit plurals file

name: units-invalid-compound-units
description: A compound unit such as m-per-s takes an SI modifier on each of its components; a modifier applied to the whole string, or a misspelled or wrongly cased component, is invalid.
common_causes: Stacking a modifier in front of an already modified component (kmm-per-s)
Spelling a component differently from its symbol (m-per-sec)
Changing the case of a component (m-per-S)
Expecting the modifier to apply to the whole compound unit rather than to one component
explanation: Compound units are built from unit symbols joined by -per- and optional ^ exponents (m-per-s, m-per-s^2, m^3). Each component may carry one SI symbol modifier, so cm-per-us and mm^3 are valid, and each component must otherwise match the schema symbol exactly.
correction_strategy: Apply one SI modifier to each component that needs one and keep every component spelled as its schema symbol

correction_examples.explanation: Only one modifier per component
Components are unit symbols; the symbol for second is s
Components are case-sensitive

correction_patterns: One modifier per component
Components are schema symbols
Exponents stay attached to their component (mm^3, s^2)
fix_instructions: 1. Split the unit on -per- into its components
2. Check each component is a schema unit symbol with at most one SI modifier in front
3. Keep any ^ exponent attached to its component
validation_hints: Match compound units component by component
A modifier belongs to a component, not to the string
cm-per-us is centimeters per microsecond

name: units-invalid-any-units
description: A placeholder with unitClass=anyUnits (Quantity in HED 8.5.0) accepts a value with or without a unit; when a unit is given it must be a valid unit of some unit class of the schema.
common_causes: Using a unit that no unit class of the schema lists or derives
Changing the case of a unit symbol (MS for ms)
Stacking two SI modifiers on one component (kmm-per-s)
explanation: The pseudo unit class anyUnits stands for every unit class of the schema. A value on such a placeholder may be a bare number (Quantity/7 is valid; unlike Delay and Duration nothing requires a unit) or a number followed by any listed unit or derived form (SI modifier, plural) of any class. With a unit, the value converts to the default unit of the class that unit belongs to when that unit has a conversionFactor; without a unit there is no default unit and no conversion, and the value is used as written. When a string is listed in one class and derived in another, the listed unit wins: dB is the decibel of intensityUnits, not d + B of memorySizeUnits. A unit that no class accepts is UNITS_INVALID as usual.
correction_strategy: Use a unit that some unit class of the schema lists or derives, spelled and cased as in the schema

correction_examples.explanation: foo is not a unit of any class
Unit symbols are case-sensitive

correction_patterns: Any unit of any class, or no unit at all
Only real units, spelled and cased as listed
Listed unit beats derived form
fix_instructions: 1. Check that the unit is a listed unit or a derived form in some unit class of the schema
2. Keep the case and spelling exactly as listed
validation_hints: A bare number is valid on an anyUnits placeholder; only a present unit is checked
Resolve the unit against every unit class when the placeholder's class is anyUnits
Prefer a listed unit over a derived form when two classes match

name: units-invalid-def-value-units
description: A Def value carries units although the definition's placeholder already has them.
common_causes: Giving units in the Def value when the definition supplies them
explanation: The value of Def/Freq/3 kHz replaces the # in (Frequency/# Hz), giving Frequency/3 kHz Hz, which has two units. A validator may report this as VALUE_INVALID, as the substituted value is not valid, or as DEF_INVALID, as the Def value has units the definition does not allow.
correction_strategy: Give only the number in the Def value

correction_examples.explanation: The definition supplies Hz

correction_patterns: Substitute the Def value into the definition and check the result
fix_instructions: 1. Find the definition's placeholder
2. If it has units, give the Def value without units
validation_hints: Check the substituted tag, not only the Def value
